title: Anchored prompt library and rollout guardrails for config/model change gating
creator: Marco Silva
description: Problem statement: We need an authoritative, versioned library of anchored (trusted) prompt sets that can be used by the eval pipeline to automatically gate configuration or model changes before they reach production. Today teams curate ad-hoc prompt lists per experiment; this causes drift in signal, duplicate effort, and missed regressions when we change tokenizer/config/quantization or swap model variants. This ticket scopes product requirements for: (1) curated anchored prompt library (AP Library) with owners, lineage, and semantic tags; (2) fine-grained ACLs and role mapping so only designated owners can promote sets to 'gating' status; (3) integration points so the CI/eval harness runs a defined regression suite when model/config change is proposed; (4) decision rules and thresholds that trigger blocking rollouts with clear remediation paths.
background: Context: Recent incidents where a quantized variant increased hallucination on system prompts highlighted the lack of stable prompt anchors across teams. Engineering already owns an eval harness (ENG-7724) and PM has proposals for dataset registries, but we lack the product-level contract describing: what constitutes an anchor prompt set, how to annotate expected outputs, how to version and pin them to rollout policies, and how to display gating decisions in Console. Goal: reduce undetected quality regressions from model/config changes by 80% for high-impact routes in Q2 2025.
acceptance_criteria: AP Library spec published and reviewed by eng + research + security
Product Console shows AP Library with version, owner, tags, and last-run eval summary
ACLs implemented so only owners can mark a set as 'gating' or 'trusted'
CI integration: any model/config change that affects customer-facing routes triggers automated evals against the selected gating sets
Decision rules codified: pass/fail thresholds (e.g., exact-match, ROUGE/BERScore thresholds, hallucination heuristics) and an unambiguous block/fallback action
Rollout UI surfaces failing prompt examples and suggested rollback or fallback model variant
A runbook for false positives and process for emergency override with audit trail
tasks: Draft AP Library data model (fields: id, name, description, owner, tags, version, canonical_examples, expected_output_annotations, approved_for_gating:boolean, lineage)
Define metadata schema for expected outputs and evaluation heuristics (annotation format)
Design Console UI for AP Library browsing, ownership transfer, and marking gating sets
Implement ACLs & RBAC hooks (tie to SSO groups) with audit logging
Wire CI: on PR/rollout proposal, trigger eval job referencing selected AP Library versions
Create gating policy DSL: threshold config, severity mapping, fallback strategies
Integrate alerts to Slack + PagerDuty for high-severity gating failures
Pilot with two product routes (chat assistant & search reranking) and measure detection rate
Document rollout remediation playbook and owner contact flow
notes: Trade-offs considered: keeping AP Library small (core anchors) vs. broad coverage. Recommendation: minimum 3 canonical prompts per high-impact route, with a separate 'exploratory' bucket for wider signal that doesn't gate automatically.
Ownership model: team-level owners with delegated curators. Promotion to 'gating' requires two approvals (owner + PM or SRE reviewer).
Versioning: semantic versioning for sets (major = semantics changed; minor = annotation tweaks). Evaluation jobs must pin to exact set version for auditability.
Cost implications: gating full evals on every PR increases infra spend—introduce sampling rules and fast heuristics for low-risk changes.
Backward compatibility: when models are retired, tool should suggest equivalent set remapping or mark dependent sets as 'orphaned'.
Proposed heuristic metrics: fidelity score (expected vs. actual), hallucination rate, response-length-delta, toxic-token-rate.
risks: False positives blocking safe rollouts — need clear override/audit path
Owner churn causing gaps in maintenance — automate owner reminders and orphan detection
Large gating sets causing long CI latency — introduce fast-path heuristics and prioritized test ordering
stakeholders: Engineering: Aisha Banerjee (runtime), Omar Patel (eval infra)
